channel.title: Taste Daily
channel.description: A daily conversation from the frontier: AI, robotics, space, compute, and the beautifully made machines and designs that shape how the future looks and feels. Hosts Hal and Samantha follow ideas out to their strange and mystical edges, and listen for the early signals of where the culture is heading.

item.title: We Sample the Superintelligence First, Like Any Good Royal Taster
item.description:
Biology rebranded as hardware, proofs getting cheap, frontier labs turning into security states, and the Musk empire racing to become one company. Plus a container tunnel, a teenage space utility, Voyager nearing one light-day, and the year the past looked like the future.
- Warhound: cloned, gene-edited military dogs: Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey's Warhound launched with a $200M seed at $1.2B to biobank, clone and gene-edit working dogs fitted with Anduril gear, pitched as Canine-as-a-Service. https://x.com/PalmerLuckey/status/2113376729998012889 https://x.com/PalmerLuckey/status/2113498161151189435 https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/ben-lamm-raises-200m-for-warhound-to-engineer-war-dogs-and-arm-them-with-anduril-gear/ https://fortune.com/2026/10/22/palmer-luckey-dire-wolfe-billionaire-lamm-warhound-200-million-dogs-cloned/ https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/warhound-launches-with-200-million-to-rebuild-americas-military-working-dog-supply-using-advanced-genetics-and-defense-technology-302917498.html - Black October, day three: formal verification at scale: Anthropic and Theorem report machine-checked no-crash proofs for 239 entry points across 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries at the RISC-V level, while Casey Handmer notes proofs remove only one of thousands of attack vectors. https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2113390212911083894 https://x.com/CJHandmer/status/2113295801409745226 https://x.com/nikitabier/status/2113391124287230296 https://www.anthropic.com/research/formal-verification https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify - OpenAI's Signal firings: The WSJ details how OpenAI fired safety researchers Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni after finding disappearing Signal messages; Daniel Kokotajlo calls it pretextual and OpenAI cites policy violations. https://x.com/DKokotajlo/status/2113474981384581431 https://x.com/AISafetyMemes/status/2113475953947287749 https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2113298833392496746 https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/the-signal-chats-that-cost-openai-researchers-their-jobs-594c5853 https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvlydn8d3lkjo - Starship Moon refueling: 22 flights or 6 to 8?: NASA's safety panel cites about 22 refueling launches for a Starship lunar landing; Elon Musk says 6 to 8, and the panel will recommend re-examining Artemis IV. https://x.com/SciGuySpace/status/2113340439893856278 https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2113377866478231647 https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/10/latest-estimate-for-starship-launches-required-to-support-a-moon-landing-22/ https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/nasa-safety-panel-concerned-about-artemis-iv-future-access-to-leo/

item.content:encoded:
Biology rebranded as hardware, proofs getting cheap, frontier labs turning into security states, and the Musk empire racing to become one company. Plus a container tunnel, a teenage space utility, Voyager nearing one light-day, and the year the past looked like the future.

  1. Warhound: cloned, gene-edited military dogs Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey's Warhound launched with a $200M seed at $1.2B to biobank, clone and gene-edit working dogs fitted with Anduril gear, pitched as Canine-as-a-Service. @PalmerLuckey · @PalmerLuckey · TechCrunch · Fortune · Press release
  2. Black October, day three: formal verification at scale Anthropic and Theorem report machine-checked no-crash proofs for 239 entry points across 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries at the RISC-V level, while Casey Handmer notes proofs remove only one of thousands of attack vectors. @AnthropicAI · @CJHandmer · @nikitabier · Anthropic research · Theorem OSS Verify
  3. OpenAI's Signal firings The WSJ details how OpenAI fired safety researchers Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni after finding disappearing Signal messages; Daniel Kokotajlo calls it pretextual and OpenAI cites policy violations. @DKokotajlo · @AISafetyMemes · @OpenAI · WSJ · BBC
  4. Starship Moon refueling: 22 flights or 6 to 8? NASA's safety panel cites about 22 refueling launches for a Starship lunar landing; Elon Musk says 6 to 8, and the panel will recommend re-examining Artemis IV. @SciGuySpace · @elonmusk · Ars Technica · SpacePolicyOnline

Signals

  • John Carmack on 50 Hz robot joint targets vs 60 Hz video: robot data capture standards are coming (medium). https://x.com/ID_AA_Carmack/status/2113328537319166349

item.title: Pilot
item.description:
Episode 0. Capability is arriving faster than the institutions around it: banks versus agents, day two of Black October, Anthropic's S-1, ten gigawatts, the personal agent wars, a fight over orthogonality, and two beautiful things made by one person each.
- Banks find agents inside customer accounts: Morgan Stanley blocks outside agents and other big banks restrict them, because fraud models can't tell an authorized agent from an account takeover; scoped, delegated credentials look like the eventual fix. https://x.com/unusual_whales/status/2113283484336918706 https://x.com/chamath/status/2113281902694330823 - Black October, day two: Model-driven vulnerability discovery has gone vertical, roon says government pressure shaped Anthropic's cyber release, and the real bottleneck is patch distribution, not finding bugs. https://x.com/nikitabier/status/2113144322870874440 https://x.com/tszzl/status/2113119644399910968 https://x.com/tszzl/status/2113117685886386578 - Anthropic's S-1 could land Friday: A reported raise of up to $100B at roughly a $2T valuation, with fast-growing revenue and an enormous compute-driven loss; the risk factors will be the read of the year. https://x.com/unusual_whales/status/2113128025638453427 - Elon Musk: a shot at exceeding 10GW next year: About a quarter of expected new US compute capacity; the binding constraint is now power and interconnect, not chips. https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2113083491835384090 - The personal agent wars: Muse, Duet, Dots and Bots: the winner may be whichever agent first gets real, scoped access to the financial system. https://x.com/signulll/status/2112993042533593423 - Is orthogonality false?: Janus argues values and capabilities may cluster, and Joscha Bach notes honesty-trained models are likelier to report consciousness. https://x.com/repligate/status/2113036473536839836 https://x.com/Plinz/status/2113036320906064066 - Slop New York: Mr.doob's procedural New York in roughly 784KB gzipped: constraint craft in the demoscene tradition. https://x.com/mrdoob/status/2113177383658561721 - A 150-megapixel Lagoon Nebula: Andrew McCarthy's backyard image of the stellar nursery in Sagittarius, integrated over weeks. https://x.com/AJamesMcCarthy/status/2113297810888237375
Signals: - Read-only agent access is the banks' opening position; expect open-banking-style scoped tokens to arrive in months, not a decade. - "Slow everything down until patching catches up" will be said seriously in a congressional hearing within weeks. - Watch whether SpaceX becomes a neocloud selling compute to rival labs, as with Anthropic on Colossus 1. - When code gets cheap, taste in what to leave out becomes the scarce skill.

item.content:encoded:
Episode 0. Capability is arriving faster than the institutions around it: banks versus agents, day two of Black October, Anthropic's S-1, ten gigawatts, the personal agent wars, a fight over orthogonality, and two beautiful things made by one person each.

  1. Banks find agents inside customer accounts Morgan Stanley blocks outside agents and other big banks restrict them, because fraud models can't tell an authorized agent from an account takeover; scoped, delegated credentials look like the eventual fix. @unusual_whales · @chamath
  2. Black October, day two Model-driven vulnerability discovery has gone vertical, roon says government pressure shaped Anthropic's cyber release, and the real bottleneck is patch distribution, not finding bugs. @nikitabier · @tszzl · @tszzl
  3. Anthropic's S-1 could land Friday A reported raise of up to $100B at roughly a $2T valuation, with fast-growing revenue and an enormous compute-driven loss; the risk factors will be the read of the year. @unusual_whales
  4. Elon Musk: a shot at exceeding 10GW next year About a quarter of expected new US compute capacity; the binding constraint is now power and interconnect, not chips. @elonmusk
  5. The personal agent wars Muse, Duet, Dots and Bots: the winner may be whichever agent first gets real, scoped access to the financial system. @signulll
  6. Is orthogonality false? Janus argues values and capabilities may cluster, and Joscha Bach notes honesty-trained models are likelier to report consciousness. @repligate · @Plinz
  7. Slop New York Mr.doob's procedural New York in roughly 784KB gzipped: constraint craft in the demoscene tradition. @mrdoob
  8. A 150-megapixel Lagoon Nebula Andrew McCarthy's backyard image of the stellar nursery in Sagittarius, integrated over weeks. @AJamesMcCarthy

Signals

  • Read-only agent access is the banks' opening position; expect open-banking-style scoped tokens to arrive in months, not a decade.
  • "Slow everything down until patching catches up" will be said seriously in a congressional hearing within weeks.
  • Watch whether SpaceX becomes a neocloud selling compute to rival labs, as with Anthropic on Colossus 1.
  • When code gets cheap, taste in what to leave out becomes the scarce skill.
